[Kayhan_online] 🔰Second Anniversary of Yahya Sinwar's Martyrdom
🔸October 16, 2026, marks…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Kayhan_online

🔰Second Anniversary of Yahya Sinwar's Martyrdom

🔸October 16, 2026, marks the second anniversary of the martyrdom of Yahya Sinwar, known as "Abu Ibrahim," former head of the political bureau of the Hamas movement — a figure whose life was intertwined with captivity and the political and military developments of Gaza.

🔸Sinwar was born in 1962 in the Khan Younis camp, into a family displaced from the city of Al-Majdal. The experience of living in the camp and the aftermath of the Nakba formed the social context for the shaping of his political outlook. He studied Arabic language at the Islamic University of Gaza and expanded his political activity in the student environment — a path that was accompanied by repeated arrests at the hands of the occupation forces.

🔸His longest period of captivity began in 1988 and continued until his release in 2011. In prison, Sinwar became one of the organizational officials of Hamas prisoners, learned Hebrew, and followed developments in the society and politics of the Zionist regime. His release in the "Wafa al-Ahrar" agreement, which led to the release of 1,027 Palestinian prisoners in exchange for the Israeli soldier "Gilad Shalit," brought the issue of prisoners more prominently into his political life.

🔸In 2017, he assumed the leadership of Hamas in the Gaza Strip and was elected for another term in 2021. After the assassination of the martyr Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran, Hamas announced on August 6, 2024, the election of Sinwar as head of the movement's political bureau — an election in the midst of war that entrusted the responsibility of political leadership of the movement to the leadership based in Gaza.

🔸Sinwar was martyred on October 16, 2024, during a clash with the forces of the occupation army in Tel al-Sultan, Rafah. The army of the Zionist regime announced his martyrdom the following day, and Hamas confirmed his martyrdom on October 18. According to published reports, the forces involved were initially unaware of his identity, and identification was carried out after the clash.

🔸Images of the final moments of the martyr Sinwar in a destroyed building in Tel al-Sultan became one of the most enduring scenes of the Gaza war — images that showed him wounded and throwing a piece of wood toward an Israeli drone.

🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram
@Kayhan_Online

🔸The series "Asbad" can be counted among those TV productions whose significance isn't limited to the story they tell. On the surface, this 24-episode series, directed by MohammadReza Moeini, is a fictional narrative about the death of a village elder, a dispute among the locals, a historical legacy, and a web of family and social relationships—but on a deeper level, it strives to bring to the television screen a region that has rarely had the chance to be seen in the full richness of its cultural, historical, and human potential.
🔸"Asbad" can be seen as an attempt to shift the angle of vision—moving away from an image that views a region solely through the lens of its problems, and drawing closer to people who, like all Iranians, have their own lives, loves, families, conflicts, aspirations, work, migration, hopes, and concerns. This shift in perspective is no small feat for television. If Iranian television is to once again play a more serious role in showcasing the country's cultural geography, works like Asbad can help pave part of that path.

Kayhan investigates 🔰 Securing gas for the northern provinces is one of the president's goals on his trip to Turkmenistan

🔸With the onset of the cold season, the gas imbalance will become apparent, especially in the north of the country; therefore, the president, who is heading to Turkmenistan today, must pursue the import and swap of gas from the northern neighbor.

🔸According to our reporter, our country, due to its vast geography and the unparalleled coverage of the household gas network, along with the dependence of power plants and various industries on gas fuel, has faced an imbalance between production and consumption. The enemy's attack on South Pars during the 40-day war, although it met with Iran's decisive and unexpected response to the gas facilities of "Ras Laffan" and caught the enemy off guard, part of the country's gas production was also damaged and the imbalances worsened.

🔸Damage to five phases of the South Pars refineries during the Ramadan war reduced the country's daily gas production capacity by about 230 million cubic meters. So far, according to the National Gas Company, 95 million cubic meters of gas have returned to the grid, and currently there is a deficit of 135 million cubic meters of gas.

🔸If the upcoming winter is similar to last year's winter in terms of temperature and consumption, and only 95 million cubic meters of the damaged capacity is restored, the gas deficit will be about 130 million cubic meters, which, combined with the previous imbalance figure, will total about 380 million cubic meters per day.

🔸The gas shortage problem is not limited to homes, and power plants, in order to prevent power outages for household subscribers, are forced to turn to alternative fuels, namely diesel and fuel oil. The increased consumption of fuel oil, or mazut, also leads to an increase in pollutants and worsening air pollution.

🔸Of course, gas imports from Turkmenistan also face obstacles. The story of gas imports from this country began with a 25-year contract concluded between the parties in 1997, but due to financial problems that arose during Bijan Zangeneh's ministry in Hassan Rouhani's government, it ran into trouble in subsequent years. Of course, the other side also had breaches of commitment, which ultimately, with the weak defense of the Iranian side in the legal dispute, resulted in our country being fined. This fine and its consequences have cast a shadow over oil transfers between the two countries in recent years.

🔸Despite all these problems, during the era of the martyred Raisi in the Thirteenth Government and with Iran's personal follow-up, Iran was able to receive the right of oil swap between Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan in the form of gas. Now the Fourteenth Government must exert all its power to renew this matter — whether in the form of swap rights or direct import.
